title: Wendell and the Spire
premise: Jonah Thornbury, once the storm-caller who broke the siege of Harrowgate and was exiled for it, has spent a decade selling rain-charms in Cinderhollow, where magic is outlawed and memory of her deeds is legally erased. When prayers to the old gods begin to be answered again, each answered prayer drains warmth from the world into the Spire beneath the mountain, where the court of the buried king keeps souls as currency—including the soul Jonah sold them ten years ago to survive. To reclaim it she must descend with a disgraced priest, a god-touched child, and the man who betrayed her, learning that the long winter falling on the world is the price of her own bargain. In the end Jonah refuses both the court's throne and the gods' demand that she become their storm again, shattering the Spire's ledger at the cost of her own memories of everyone she loves—surviving, finally, at a price she chooses.
about_author: Sebastian Reyes is the pen name of a former archivist who spent six years cataloguing folk charms in mountain villages before turning to fiction. They write fantasy about bargains, forgetting, and the people history decides not to remember.

chapters.title: The Charm Seller
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. In outlawed Cinderhollow, Jonah sells a luck-knot to a dying woman and feels her own magic stir unwantedly. Establishes her careful invisibility and loneliness. Emotional beat: the ache of a life shrunk small enough to be safe.

chapters.title: First Answered Prayer
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. A child prays to the old god Vessia at a cracked shrine—and something answers, frost blooming across the whole street. Jonah recognizes the signature of power she thought dead. Beat: wonder curdling into dread.

chapters.title: The Graycloaks Come
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The magic-inquisitors raid the market tracing the miracle; Jonah hides her brand-scarred wrists while an old friend is taken instead. Guilt and the cost of staying hidden. Beat: survival as complicity.

chapters.title: What the Ledger Owes
chapters.summary: Disgraced priest Anselm's POV. Anselm, keeper of a defunct order's records, finds Jonah's name in a soul-ledger fragment: sold to the court beneath the mountain, payment dated the night of Harrowgate. He seeks her out. Beat: the past refusing to stay buried.

chapters.title: Ten Years Ago
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV, interwoven flashback. The siege of Harrowgate: her storm saved ten thousand lives, the price was a soul pledged to the buried king, and her lover Cassian testified against her. Beat: love and betrayal braided together.

chapters.title: The God-Touched Girl
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. A feral child who hears the old gods speaking through cracks in the world attaches herself to Jonah, reciting Jonah's own forgotten true name. Beat: being known is terrifying and irresistible.

chapters.title: Winter's First Teeth
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The first snow falls in high summer; crops blacken; refugees arrive claiming the cold follows answered prayers. Jonah realizes every miracle feeds the Spire. Beat: dawning scale of the catastrophe.

chapters.title: Cassian at the Gate
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Cassian arrives in Cinderhollow as the crown's envoy negotiating with the Spire's court—he has spent ten years serving it to keep his family alive. Confrontation, old wounds opened. Beat: hatred complicated by unfinished love.

chapters.title: The Road Beneath
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. The company—Jonah, Wren, Anselm, and a coerced Cassian—descends the pilgrim road into the mountain's roots, pursued by Graycloaks and hunted by things wearing the faces of the dead. Beat: commitment past the point of return.

chapters.title: Vessia's Hunger
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. At a drowned shrine, the goddess Vessia speaks through Wren: the gods are not returning—they are escaping the Spire, and they will burn the world to do it. Beat: allies revealed as another kind of threat.

chapters.title: The Court of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. They reach the outer court beneath the mountain: gilded, frozen, populated by souls who traded themselves willingly and smile forever. Jonah sees what her sale purchased. Beat: horror dressed as comfort.

chapters.title: The Price of the Siege
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Cassian confesses the full truth: he testified to save his sister from the ledger, and he has been quietly buying back stolen souls ever since. Jonah must decide whether betrayal can be paid down like debt. Beat: forgiveness as a choice, not a feeling.

chapters.title: Audience with the Buried King
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The king offers Jonah her soul back if she takes the throne beside him—the winter ends only if someone holds the ledger and enforces its debts. Beat: temptation framed as mercy.

chapters.title: What Wren Remembers
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren reveals she is a returned soul, one the ledger spat back incomplete; the gods speak through her because she is a crack herself. She begs Jonah not to trade anyone for her. Beat: innocence carrying the book's moral weight.

chapters.title: The Graycloak Verdict
chapters.summary: Anselm's POV. Graycloaks breach the court; Anselm burns the order's records to cover the company's escape and is captured in exchange. Beat: sacrifice by a man redeeming a lifetime of obedience.

chapters.title: Storm Without a Caller
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Fleeing upward, Jonah tries to call a storm to seal the passage behind them and cannot—the gods have withdrawn their permission, revealing her power was always borrowed. Beat: identity stripped to nothing.

chapters.title: The Ledger's Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Cassian deciphers the ledger: the winter isn't punishment but collection—the world's warmth is the interest owed on every answered prayer since the gods fled. Destroying the ledger voids all debts, including Jonah's soul. Beat: hope with a terrible fine print.

chapters.title: Descent Again
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. The company turns back into the mountain voluntarily, through the frozen court, while the gods scream through Wren to stop them—they need the ledger intact to escape. Beat: choosing the hard right over the easy wrong.

chapters.title: The Breaking of the Book
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Climax. On the Spire's heart, Jonah wrestles the buried king, refuses the throne, and shatters the ledger—but the ledger demands a binding from the breaker, and it takes her memories of everyone she loves. Beat: triumph and loss in the same stroke.

chapters.title: Thaw
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. Winter breaks; the old gods fade gently into weather and seasons rather than escape or dominion; Anselm walks out of the court freed by the voided debts. Beat: relief shadowed by grief.

chapters.title: The Woman Who Sold the Rain
chapters.summary: Cassian's POV. Cassian tends Jonah, who no longer knows him, and begins telling her their story from the beginning, one day at a time. Wren stays near, half-goddess, wholly loved. Beat: love as re-giving what was lost.

chapters.title: Charm Seller, Twice Made
chapters.summary: Jonah's POV. Spring in Cinderhollow: Jonah sells small charms again, feeling echoes of feelings she can't name when certain customers pass. She chooses, knowingly this time, a small life—not from fear, but freely. Final beat: survival's price paid, and worth it.
